9	import { API_ERROR_MESSAGE, EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants';
10	// Zimmermann's own constant — NOT the base package above (see recommended-products/index.tsx's
11	// own comment on this exact gotcha: a named import off the base package's untyped module compiles
12	// but is undefined at runtime). APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX, not PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX — this page has no
13	// PageContainer/layerStyle second containment layer for PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX to correctly
14	// cancel; see that constant's own comment in app/constants/index.ts for the bug this distinction
15	// fixes (a real, live-confirmed horizontal overflow, Marcel, 2026-09-10).
16	import { APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX } from 'app/constants';
17	import { ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid } from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid';
18	import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
19	import {
20	  selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard,
21	  resolveOrderableVariant,
22	} from '../../utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard';
23	import type {
24	  RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard,
25	  RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
26	} from '../../utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard';
27	
28	// Message-id namespace follows this codebase's existing `<page>.<category>.<key>` convention
29	// (see home.*, product_list.*, product_detail.* in their own index.tsx files) -- `recently_viewed`
30	// is this page's own snake_case prefix.
31	const messages = defineMessages({
32	  title: {
33	    id: 'recently_viewed.heading.title',
34	    defaultMessage: 'Recently Viewed',
35	  },
36	  // Real ICU `plural` selector, not string interpolation -- decided explicitly this session
37	  // (build plan §B1, "go for it" -- Marcel, 2026-09-08). `#` is replaced by the matched `count`
38	  // value at each branch, so this renders "1 item" / "16 items" correctly with no separate
39	  // singular-check needed at the call site. Lowercase "item(s)" -- corrected 2026-09-11 (Marcel).
40	  itemCount: {
41	    id: 'recently_viewed.label.item_count',
42	    defaultMessage: '{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}',
43	  },
44	  emptyHeading: {
45	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.heading',
46	    defaultMessage: "You haven't viewed anything yet.",
47	  },
48	  emptyBodyRegistered: {
49	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.body_registered',
50	    defaultMessage: 'Continue shopping to start building your history.',
51	  },
52	  emptyBodyGuest: {
53	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.body_guest',
54	    defaultMessage: 'Sign in to keep track of your history, or continue shopping.',
55	  },
56	  continueShopping: {
57	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.cta.continue_shopping',
58	    defaultMessage: 'Continue Shopping',
59	  },
60	  signIn: {
61	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.cta.sign_in',
62	    defaultMessage: 'Sign In',
63	  },
64	  // Same copy, same event, as product-list/index.tsx's own `product_list.toast.added_to_bag` --
65	  // a distinct message id under this page's own `recently_viewed.*` namespace (see this file's own
66	  // message-id-namespace comment above) rather than importing that page's message across a page
67	  // boundary.
68	  addedToBag: {
69	    id: 'recently_viewed.toast.added_to_bag',
70	    defaultMessage: 'Added to bag',
71	  },
72	});
73	
74	// Plain literal, not run through react-intl -- matches home/index.tsx's own un-translated Seo
75	// `description` precedent (`description="Commerce Cloud Retail React App"`). The build plan's
76	// SEO section only calls out `title` for useIntl; this page's own description copy was never
77	// specified, so it is authored here rather than invented as a translated message with no source.
78	const PAGE_DESCRIPTION = "Browse the products you've recently viewed at Zimmermann.";
79	
80	type EmptyRecentlyViewedProps = {
81	  isRegistered: boolean;
82	};
83	
84	/**
85	 * SFCC-84's own empty-state design (build plan §B2 "Empty state"). There is no AC or Figma design
86	 * for this state at all; copy and structure are ported from the real `EmptyCart` precedent
87	 * (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/partials/empty-cart.jsx`), per
88	 * Marcel's own direction ("look for a pattern in the existing codebase and build off that"): a
89	 * `Box` > `Center` > `Stack` layout, an `isRegistered`-branched body message, and a
90	 * `Button as={Link}` CTA pattern (the base SFCC `Link`, not a raw `react-router-dom` one, so the
91	 * "Continue Shopping"/"Sign In" hrefs get this storefront's real multi-site URL prefixing --
92	 * `use-multi-site.js`'s `buildUrl`, called internally by that `Link` -- the same reason `EmptyCart`
93	 * itself uses it).
94	 *
95	 * **Deliberately not a byte-for-byte styling port.** `EmptyCart`'s own prop values
96	 * (`fontSize={['18px', '2xl']}`, `color="gray.700"`, `color="blue.600"`,
97	 * `width={['343px', '220px']}`) are raw base-Chakra literals with no relationship to Zimmermann's
98	 * design tokens, and this codebase's styling hierarchy
99	 * (`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`) requires `textStyle`/`var(--zimm-*)` for new
100	 * Zimmermann-authored UI and forbids a raw px/rem literal outright. With no confirmed empty-state
101	 * Figma spec to derive exact values from, this uses the nearest reasonable *registered* tokens
102	 * (`heading2`/`body1` text styles, `text-default`/`text-secondary` colours, `2xl`/`2xs`/`m`
103	 * spacing) instead -- an autonomous styling judgement call (see this module's own bottom-of-file
104	 * decision log), not a design decision that conflicts with an existing one (there is no existing
105	 * design here to conflict with).
106	 *
107	 * **No icon.** `EmptyCart` renders `BasketIcon` above its heading and `AccountIcon` on its
108	 * "Sign In" button. Checked directly against `overrides/app/components/icons`' full export list:
109	 * no Recently-Viewed-thematic icon exists (no eye/clock/history glyph), and forcing an unrelated
110	 * one -- `BasketIcon` itself, or reusing `AccountIcon` -- would misrepresent this page rather than
111	 * help it, so both are omitted; heading + copy + CTA(s) alone still satisfies the established
112	 * empty-state pattern this page is following.
113	 *
114	 * `useIntl` is called directly in this leaf, not passed down as a prop -- this is the
115	 * Context-backed, app-wide exception `.claude/rules/components.md` > Composition documents for
116	 * `useIntl`/`useUiCopy` specifically (this is a private, single-parent sub-component of this page,
117	 * not a component exported from its own folder, so it needs no story/test of its own either --
118	 * its behaviour is exercised through this page's own `index.test.tsx`).
119	 */
120	const EmptyRecentlyViewed = ({ isRegistered }: EmptyRecentlyViewedProps) => {
121	  const intl = useIntl();
122	
123	  return (
124	    <Box data-testid="recently-viewed-empty">
125	      <Center>
126	        <Stack spacing="var(--zimm-scale-2xl)" textAlign="center" paddingY="var(--zimm-scale-4xl)">
127	          <Stack spacing="var(--zimm-scale-2xs)">
128	            <Text textStyle="heading2" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">
129	              {intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyHeading)}
130	            </Text>
131	            <Text textStyle="body1" color="var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)">
132	              {isRegistered
133	                ? intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyBodyRegistered)
134	                : intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyBodyGuest)}
135	            </Text>
136	          </Stack>
137	          <Stack direction={{ base: 'column', sm: 'row' }} justify="center" spacing="var(--zimm-scale-m)">
138	            {/* Continue Shopping is the loud/primary CTA for a registered shopper (their only
139	                CTA), but yields primary emphasis to Sign In for a guest -- same isRegistered-driven
140	                emphasis flip EmptyCart's own solid/outline split encodes, re-expressed here via
141	                ZimmButton's own primary/secondary variants instead of a raw colour override. */}
142	            <Button
143	              as={Link}
144	              href="/"
145	              variant={isRegistered ? 'primary' : 'secondary'}
146	              width={{ base: 'full', sm: 'auto' }}
147	            >
148	              {intl.formatMessage(messages.continueShopping)}
149	            </Button>
150	            {!isRegistered && (
151	              <Button as={Link} href="/account" variant="primary" width={{ base: 'full', sm: 'auto' }}>
152	                {intl.formatMessage(messages.signIn)}
153	              </Button>
154	            )}
155	          </Stack>
156	        </Stack>
157	      </Center>
158	    </Box>
159	  );
160	};
161	
162	/**
163	 * SFCC-84 -- Recently Viewed Full History page container (build plan §B2, rewired to real Einstein
164	 * data by build plan step E2). Thin container: calls `useEinstein()` directly, fires
165	 * `getRecommendations(EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED)` once on mount, reads
166	 * `recommendations.recs` off that same hook once the request resolves, maps each rec through the
167	 * unchanged `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` (filtering the hard `null` gate every mapper in
168	 * this codebase uses), and renders `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` -- or, with no recs, this page's own
169	 * empty state (`EmptyRecentlyViewed` above). Matches `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own
170	 * Recently-Viewed branch exactly (build plan step E1, already committed) -- same
171	 * `useEinstein()`/`getRecommendations`/`recommendations.recs` chain, same unmodified mapper family,
172	 * just this page's own container instead of that shared rail.
173	 *
174	 * **Replaces the interim, browser-tracked view-history hook and its companion product-fetch
175	 * utility this page previously shipped with** (scheduled for deletion in build plan step E4, not
176	 * yet run as of this commit -- this page no longer references either one, but the files still
177	 * exist on disk pending that step; see `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own module docblock,
178	 * which names them directly, for the full "why" of that interim build and why it is superseded
179	 * now). `recommendations.recs` is a strict
180	 * superset of the plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` shape the interim build fed this same
181	 * mapper (Einstein's own `fetchRecProductDetails`, `use-einstein.js:465-520`, already merges each
182	 * rec with its full hydrated `getProducts` record before this component ever sees it), so
183	 * `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` needed no change at all -- confirmed directly against that
184	 * function's body, not assumed.
185	 *
186	 * **Known, already-flagged gap, not introduced here:** `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`'s
187	 * `badge` field is always `undefined` -- the plain `getProducts` endpoint this build reads from has
188	 * no confirmed `c_productBadges` field (see that mapper's own docblock's "Badge" section). A card
189	 * rendered by this page will never show a badge yet; this is a pre-existing, out-of-scope gap for
190	 * this step, not a bug in this file.
191	 *
192	 * **Empty-state gate, race-safe (build plan step E2, decision #3):** `recs.length > 0` renders the
193	 * grid; `!isLoading && recs.length === 0` renders `EmptyRecentlyViewed`; anything else (i.e.
194	 * `isLoading` still `true`, request in flight, no recs yet) renders neither -- the same principle
195	 * `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own `!recommendations?.recs?.length` gate already applies
196	 * (build plan step E1), just split into two named branches here because this page, unlike that
197	 * rail, has a real, visible empty-state component that must not flash for a shopper who does have
198	 * history. Gating on `cards.length === 0` (the post-mapping, filtered count) instead of
199	 * `recs.length` (the raw Einstein count) would risk exactly that flash while
200	 * `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` is still filtering what could still turn out to be a
201	 * fully-populated `recs` array -- gating on `recs.length` directly, ahead of that mapping step,
202	 * avoids it. The one residual case this still can't distinguish from a genuine empty history --
203	 * every returned rec failing to map (e.g. every product now offline/deleted) -- is the same
204	 * accepted edge case the pre-revision hook-based gate already carried: `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`
205	 * renders `null` for an empty `cards` array by its own documented contract, so that narrow case
206	 * renders blank content rather than either this page's populated grid or its own empty-state copy.
207	 * Not solved here, not new here.
208	 *
209	 * **First-paint window, inherited from `useEinstein()` itself, not new here:** `isLoading` and
210	 * `recommendations` both start at `false`/`[]` (`use-einstein.js:462-463`) on every render,
211	 * including the server-rendered one and this component's very first client render, before the
212	 * mount effect below has had any chance to run -- so, same as the pre-revision hook-based design
213	 * this replaces (that hook's own `useState` initial values were equally empty on first render),
214	 * there is a real window on first paint where this gate reads "not loading, zero recs" and renders
215	 * `EmptyRecentlyViewed`, until the effect fires and flips `isLoading` to `true`. Unlike the
216	 * pre-revision design, that fix-up was a synchronous `Storage` read (imperceptible); this one is a
217	 * real network round-trip (`getRecommendations` -> Einstein -> `getProducts` hydration), so the
218	 * window is not instant -- named here rather than left as a silent, undocumented regression. This
219	 * is a property of `useEinstein()`'s own initial state, not something this container introduces or
220	 * can resolve without changing that base SFCC hook (out of scope for this step).
221	 *
222	 * **SEO -- `noindex, nofollow`, via `Seo`'s `children`, not its `noIndex` prop.** Base `Seo`
223	 * (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo/index.jsx:20`) emits
224	 * `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` for `noIndex` -- `noindex` only, never `nofollow`.
225	 * Passing both `noIndex` and an explicit `<meta name="robots">` child would emit two competing
226	 * `robots` tags, so `noIndex` is left unset and the full directive is passed as a child instead
227	 * (Marcel's explicit decision, build plan §B2). `<Seo>` is otherwise mounted exactly as
228	 * `home/index.tsx` mounts it -- `title`/`description` only, no extra props.
229	 *
230	 * `getTemplateName` matches the convention already used by every other page-level override
231	 * (`home`, `product-detail`, `product-list`, `experience`, `contentful-preview` -- see each file's
232	 * own `<Page>.getTemplateName = () => '<name>';` line, placed the same way here).
233	 */
234	const RecentlyViewed = () => {
235	  const intl = useIntl();
236	  const { isRegistered } = useCustomerType();
237	  const { isLoading, recommendations, getRecommendations } = useEinstein();
238	  const toast = useToast();
239	  const { addItemToNewOrExistingBasket } = useShopperBasketsMutationHelper();
240	
241	  // Fires once on mount -- matches recommended-products/index.tsx's own Recently-Viewed branch
242	  // (build plan step E1), which fires the identical call for the identical recommender, just from
243	  // an effect with a wider dependency array (that component also handles other recommenders/zones
244	  // sharing one effect). This page only ever renders this one recommender, so an empty dependency
245	  // array is the direct equivalent -- `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` is off repo-wide
246	  // (@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/eslint/partials/react.js:26), and this exact
247	  // fire-once-on-mount-with-no-deps pattern already has a precedent needing no lint suppression:
248	  // home/index.tsx's own `useEffect(() => { einstein.sendViewPage(pathname); }, []);`.
249	  useEffect(() => {
250	    getRecommendations(EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED);
251	  }, []);
252	
253	  // Same split product-list/productListCardMapper.ts's and recommended-products/index.tsx's own
254	  // consumers already use: formatPrice is injected into the mapper rather than formatted inside
255	  // it, keeping that mapper free of any react-intl dependency of its own.
256	  const formatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string): string =>
257	    intl.formatNumber(amount, { style: 'currency', currency });
258	
259	  // Size-aware Add to Bag (2026-09-09 full-parity-with-PLP build) -- keyed by product id rather
260	  // than product-list/index.tsx's own per-card `ProductListCard` wrapper with local `useState`:
261	  // that pattern needs a per-card component instance to own its own state, but this page's grid
262	  // (`ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`) is a shared, already-shipped organism that renders `cards` directly
263	  // with no per-card wrapper slot of its own (unlike PLP, which builds its own grid inline with
264	  // full control) -- touching that organism's contract to add one would be a bigger, cross-cutting
265	  // change than this fix calls for (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5: never refactor upward). A single
266	  // id-keyed map at this container achieves the same "each card remembers its own selected size"
267	  // result without touching the Grid at all.
268	  const [selectedSizeChipValues, setSelectedSizeChipValues] = useState<Record<string, string | undefined>>({});
269	
270	  const handleResolvedAddToBag = (orderableProductId: string, price: number | undefined) => {
271	    addItemToNewOrExistingBasket([{ productId: orderableProductId, price, quantity: 1 }])
272	      .then(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(messages.addedToBag), status: 'success' }))
273	      .catch(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE), status: 'error' }));
274	  };
275	
276	  // Normalized to a real array so every `recs.length`/`recs.map` reference below is safe without
277	  // repeating the optional chain at each call site -- `useEinstein()`'s own `recommendations`
278	  // state starts as a plain `[]` (use-einstein.js:463), which has no `.recs` property at all, so
279	  // `recommendations?.recs` reads `undefined` until the request above resolves.
280	  const recs: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct[] = recommendations?.recs ?? [];
281	
282	  const cards: ZimmProductCardProps[] = recs
283	    .map((product): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
284	      const card = selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard(product, formatPrice);
285	      if (!card) return null;
286	
287	      const selectedSizeChipValue = selectedSizeChipValues[product.id];
288	      return {
289	        ...card,
290	        selectedSizeChipValue,
291	        onSizeChipSelect: (value: string) =>
292	          setSelectedSizeChipValues((previous) => ({ ...previous, [product.id]: value })),
293	        onAddToBag: () => {
294	          // No selection -> default-variant behaviour (matches product-list/index.tsx's own
295	          // ProductListCard.handleAddToBag exactly): no size selected means default size. A
296	          // selection that somehow matches no real variant falls back the same way, rather than
297	          // blocking the add entirely on a data mismatch.
298	          const resolved = selectedSizeChipValue ? resolveOrderableVariant(product, selectedSizeChipValue) : null;
299	          handleResolvedAddToBag(resolved?.productId ?? product.id, resolved?.price ?? product.price);
300	        },
301	      };
302	    })
303	    .filter((card): card is RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard => card !== null);
304	
305	  const title = intl.formatMessage(messages.title);
306	
307	  return (
308	    <Box data-testid="recently-viewed-page">
309	      <Seo title={title} description={PAGE_DESCRIPTION}>
310	        <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow" />
311	      </Seo>
312	      {/* Screen-reader-only page heading — 2026-09-10, closing a real gap: this page had no
313	       * Heading element at all in either branch below, breaking the pattern product-list/index.tsx
314	       * and product-detail/index.tsx both already follow, and leaving up to
315	       * RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED real <h3> product-name headings (ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid)
316	       * with nothing above them in the heading hierarchy (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.3.1/2.4.6). `srOnly`,
317	       * matching product-detail/index.tsx's own <h1> exactly — the page's own visible title
318	       * styling (ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid's own textStyle="heading3" span, unchanged here) is a
319	       * separate, wider pre-existing pattern (several other organisms do the same thing) and out
320	       * of scope for this fix. */}
321	      <Heading as="h1" srOnly>
322	        {title}
323	      </Heading>
324	      {recs.length > 0 ? (
325	        // Bleeds the grid edge-to-edge past #app-main's own sitewide padding, matching the
326	        // Recently Viewed Rail's own flush treatment (product-detail/product-list's
327	        // <RecommendedProducts mx={PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX}>) — confirmed against this page's own
328	        // three real Figma frames (9551:78221 Desktop / 9560:137688 Tablet / 9560:138459 Mobile,
329	        // Zimmermann_Designs file), which show the header and every Product Card Group spanning
330	        // the full frame width, not inset within a page margin. ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid itself has
331	        // no passthrough/mx slot (unlike RecommendedProducts, which forwards `{...props}` to its
332	        // own wrapping Box for exactly this reason), so the bleed is applied here at the page
333	        // level instead. EmptyRecentlyViewed below is a distinct, centred layout with no
334	        // edge-to-edge requirement of its own — deliberately not wrapped the same way.
335	        //
336	        // APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX, not PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX — corrected 2026-09-10 (real, live-confirmed
337	        // bug: this page rendered wider than the viewport at every breakpoint, e.g. 1504px at a
338	        // 1440px Desktop viewport). This page has no PageContainer/layerStyle="page" second
339	        // containment layer the way PDP/PLP do — #app-main's own padding is the only thing here to
340	        // cancel — so it needs the single-layer constant, not the two-layer one. See that
341	        // constant's own comment in app/constants/index.ts for the full root-cause math.
342	        <Box
343	          mx={APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX}
344	          // Space before the global Footer — Figma's own page frames (see the mx comment above
345	          // for the node ids) show this filled by "Footer Primary" (node 9560:110769 on Desktop,
346	          // same shape on Tablet/Mobile — a "Load More" button, deferred: real, Figma-annotated
347	          // functional requirement, not built yet, Marcel 2026-09-10), uniformly 32px top-padding +
348	          // 52px button + 80px bottom-padding = 164px on all three breakpoints, sitting flush
349	          // against both the last card row above it and the real Footer below it (zero extra gap
350	          // either side, confirmed directly). With no button to render, only the padding portion
351	          // is reserved here (32+80=112px, Marcel's own call, 2026-09-10) — not the button's own
352	          // 52px, since there's nothing occupying that height right now. This will need to grow by
353	          // that 52px once Load More is actually built; that future component replaces this
354	          // padding entirely rather than sitting alongside it.
355	          paddingBottom="calc(var(--zimm-scale-800) + var(--zimm-scale-5xl))" // 32px + 80px = 112px
356	        >
357	          <ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid
358	            title={title}
359	            itemCountLabel={intl.formatMessage(messages.itemCount, { count: cards.length })}
360	            cards={cards}
361	          />
362	        </Box>
363	      ) : !isLoading && recs.length === 0 ? (
364	        <EmptyRecentlyViewed isRegistered={isRegistered} />
365	      ) : null}
366	    </Box>
367	  );
368	};
369	
370	RecentlyViewed.getTemplateName = () => 'recently-viewed';
371	
372	export default RecentlyViewed;

8	/*
9	 * Copy-first port of
10	 * node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products/index.jsx
11	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule.
12	 *
13	 * The differences from the base file are the TypeScript annotations below and house
14	 * formatting — no changed JSX, hook calls, prop names, or reordered `useEffect`s, and the base
15	 * file's own dead check (`recommendations.length < 1` on what is always an object) is ported
16	 * byte-identical in behaviour. The annotations: a `RecommendedProductsProps` type replacing the
17	 * `propTypes` block; a narrow local `RecommendedProduct` type for the one field read off a
18	 * recommendation-context product (reused for the `productTileProps` callback's own `product`
19	 * param below, since it is that same recommendation-context product); an explicit `boolean`
20	 * param on the one nested callback that isn't contextually typed; and inline
21	 * `{ productId?: string }` / `{ id?: string }` object-type-literal params on four
22	 * `.find`/`.some`/`.map` callbacks whose containing expression is untyped (`any`) and therefore
23	 * supplies no contextual parameter type — `noImplicitAny` flags these regardless of the `any`
24	 * receiver (confirmed against `npx tsc --noEmit`, which is why these four are annotated despite
25	 * this file's own initial plan expecting two of them not to need it). The `{ productId?: string
26	 * }` shape and inline-annotation style mirrors the existing precedent at
27	 * product-detail/index.tsx:437 and :735; the `{ id?: string }` shape matches the field the base
28	 * hook itself reads, `use-einstein.js`'s own `reco.recs?.map((rec) => rec.id)` (line 466).
29	 *

/*
 * Copy-first port of
 * node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products/index.jsx
 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule.
 *
 * The differences from the base file are the TypeScript annotations below and house
 * formatting — no changed JSX, hook calls, prop names, or reordered `useEffect`s, and the base
 * file's own dead check (`recommendations.length < 1` on what is always an object) is ported
 * byte-identical in behaviour. The annotations: a `RecommendedProductsProps` type replacing the
 * `propTypes` block; a narrow local `RecommendedProduct` type for the one field read off a
 * recommendation-context product (reused for the `productTileProps` callback's own `product`
 * param below, since it is that same recommendation-context product); an explicit `boolean`
 * param on the one nested callback that isn't contextually typed; and inline
 * `{ productId?: string }` / `{ id?: string }` object-type-literal params on four
 * `.find`/`.some`/`.map` callbacks whose containing expression is untyped (`any`) and therefore
 * supplies no contextual parameter type — `noImplicitAny` flags these regardless of the `any`
 * receiver (confirmed against `npx tsc --noEmit`, which is why these four are annotated despite
 * this file's own initial plan expecting two of them not to need it). The `{ productId?: string
 * }` shape and inline-annotation style mirrors the existing precedent at
 * product-detail/index.tsx:437 and :735; the `{ id?: string }` shape matches the field the base
 * hook itself reads, `use-einstein.js`'s own `reco.recs?.map((rec) => rec.id)` (line 466).
 *
 * A sixth adjustment, found by lint rather than tsc: the base file destructures `formatMessage`
 * straight off `useIntl()`, but `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method` flags any destructured
 * reference to it — `formatMessage` is declared with method-shorthand syntax in
 * `@formatjs/intl/src/types.d.ts:64-65`, which this rule always flags regardless of whether the
 * real implementation needs `this`. Fix: keep the whole object (`const intl = useIntl();`) and
 * call `intl.formatMessage(...)` at each of its five call sites instead of destructuring — a
 * property-access call sidesteps the rule entirely, with zero behavioural change. Same
 * "toolchain requires a different access shape than the untyped base file used" reasoning as the
 * annotations above.
 *
 * SFCC-83/84 — this branch renders `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` instead of `ProductScroller` when
 * `recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'`, the
 * same string `CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED` resolves to — confirmed identical in
 * node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:156,160). Every other recommender
 * keeps the original `ProductScroller` branch below, untouched.
 *
 * **Build plan step E1 (2026-09-15) wires this branch to real Einstein data**, replacing an
 * interim browser-tracked mechanism (shipped as draft PR #107) that existed only because Einstein
 * was confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site. That interim build tracked viewed
 * product ids in local storage and fetched real product data for them via a dedicated utility —
 * both deleted in build plan step E4 — instead of ever reading `useEinstein()`'s own
 * `recommendations`. This branch now matches the other four recommenders in this same file
 * exactly:
 * 1. The `getRecommendations`/`getZoneRecommendations` effect below fires unconditionally for
 *    this recommender too — no more early return for it.
 * 2. Cards are built by mapping `recommendations.recs` through the unchanged
 *    `selectRecentlyViewedCard`. Einstein's own `fetchRecProductDetails`
 *    (use-einstein.js:465 onward) already merges each rec with its full hydrated `getProducts`
 *    record before this component ever sees it (`{...rec, ...product, productId, image}`), so
 *    every field `selectRecentlyViewedCard` reads (`id`/`name`/`imageGroups`/`variants`/`price`/
 *    `currency`) is present — a strict superset of the plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` shape
 *    the interim build fed it, confirmed directly against that function's body rather than
 *    assumed.
 * 3. The empty-state gate (AC 8) is now `!recommendations?.recs?.length` directly. This one check
 *    owns both the loading case (`useEinstein()`'s own `useState([])` initial value,
 *    use-einstein.js:463, means `recs` is `undefined` until the request resolves) and the true
 *    zero-history case. This branch still sits ahead of the base dead-check below — inherited from
 *    the interim build's own ordering — though it no longer strictly matters either way, since
 *    every path inside this `if` returns (null or the rail) and never falls through; there's just
 *    no reason to move it.
 *

## Verdict: PASS — SFCC-83+84 Einstein build plan step E2 (`overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` + `.test.tsx`)

**Round 1.** No prior REWORK on E2 in this thread.

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Correctness** | PASS | `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0, run fresh by me just now on the current working tree (including Marcel's docblock edit). `npx vitest run overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx` → 11/11 green, run fresh by me just now (the `MISSING_TRANSLATION` stderr lines are pre-existing react-intl fallback noise from an untouched message block, not a failure). Combined with the tester's already-run full suite (87 files/1324 tests green) on the pre-edit diff, and my confirmation the only delta since is comment-only, there's no correctness gap. |
| **Pass criteria** | PASS | All 5 stated E2 criteria checked with fresh, non-inherited evidence: `tsc` 0 (re-run), zero-hit grep for both dead hook names in *both* changed files (re-run, exit 1 = no match), race-safe gate proven-to-fail-first (tester's actual mutation test — changed the condition, watched the named test fail, restored, confirmed byte-identical, re-ran green — not re-derived by me since the gate line wasn't touched by the later edit), Add-to-Bag assertions confirmed unchanged byte-for-byte in the diff, `npm run test` green (composite of tester's full run + my fresh file run covering the only post-run delta). |
| **Design fidelity** | PASS (inapplicable, not blindly assumed) | Read the full current file: zero JSX structure, token, spacing, or Chakra-prop change anywhere in this diff — every visual line (`APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX`, the 112px footer padding, `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` props, `EmptyRecentlyViewed`) is untouched. The only change is the data source and the branch *condition*, not the rendered output itself. Per the plan's own stated ceiling, no live/Figma checkpoint is owed here — and I confirmed that's actually true of this diff, not just asserted by the plan. |
| **Conformance** | PASS | `useEinstein`/`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS` imported from the base package path — correct, since neither is overridden (checked: no `overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.ts` exists). Recommender referenced only via the named constant, never a string literal, per plan + conventions.md. `import type` used correctly for the two type-only imports. Page-level data-fetching is exempt from the components.md container/presentational split (that rule scopes to `overrides/app/components/`, not `overrides/app/pages/`) — calling `useEinstein()` directly here is exactly what the rule expects of a page container. |
| **Completeness** | PASS | Test file rewritten, all 11 original cases kept, AC8 (empty state) confirmed at rest, AC7 (cross-device) correctly left as an unverifiable-pre-deployment data claim per the plan's own stated ceiling — not a gap this step could close. No story exists for this page folder (confirmed: only `index.tsx`/`index.test.tsx` in the directory) — this predates E2 (never existed under the interim B2 build either) and the plan's own "no new stories, no story edits" scale call (§2), while naming `recommended-products` explicitly rather than this page by name, gives reasoning (hook-driven container, no new rendered state) that plainly extends here too. Manufacturing a story now would be restoring machinery the plan deliberately dropped, not closing a gap E2 created. |
| **Restraint** | PASS | Orchestrator's IN SCOPE verdict + my own `git status`/`git diff --stat` re-run: exactly the 2 manifest files touched, nothing else in the working tree. Marcel's own post-hoc docblock edit is a direct, minimal fix to a flag the orchestrator itself raised — not scope creep. |

**Overall: PASS**

## What I tried to falsify

- **The docblock fix "resolves the flag"** — read the live file at `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx:174-184` myself rather than trusting the paraphrase, and cross-checked its claim ("files still exist on disk pending [E4]") against the actual filesystem (`ls` on both hook files — they're still there, unmodified, Sep 15 01:25). Survives.
- **"Zero interim-hook references"** — re-ran the grep myself, fresh, against the current state of both changed files (not the tester's pre-edit snapshot). Zero hits, confirmed independently.
- **"The docblock edit is comment-only"** — read the full diff hunk rather than accepting the self-report; confirmed every changed line in that region sits inside a `/** */` block, no executable statement touched.
- **"Nothing else changed in the working tree"** — ran `git status --porcelain` and `--untracked-files=all` myself; matches the described 2-file diff exactly, no surprises.
- **"Matches E1's pattern exactly"** — read E1's already-committed `recommended-products/index.tsx` directly rather than accepting the cross-reference at face value; the `useEinstein`/`getRecommendations`/`recommendations.recs` chain and the "no seed products" reasoning do genuinely match. This is also how I found the one thing below.
- **Did not re-attempt** the tester's race-safe-gate mutation test myself — the line it covers (`index.tsx:363`) is untouched by the only edit made since that test ran, so re-running it would be re-checking a check against a diff that hasn't changed in the relevant place.

## What I could not verify

- **Live Einstein response shape** — undeployed everywhere reachable; this is the plan's own stated ceiling, not a gap in this score.
- **AC7 (cross-device restore)** — a data-source claim, unverifiable pre-deployment, per the plan and the tester's own note.
- **`npm run lint` / `audit:tokens`** — not run by me; E2's own stated pass criteria (loop-config table) don't call for them at this step, they're reserved for E4's full-gate sweep. Not treating their absence as a gap given the plan's own scale call.

## Each defect

None blocking. One non-blocking, out-of-E2's-scope observation below.

## Single biggest residual risk in shipping this step

Everything proving `recs.length > 0` renders correctly is a hand-built Vitest fixture — the actual shape Einstein returns in production (via `fetchRecProductDetails`'s merge of `{...rec, ...product, productId, image}`) has never been observed live, because Einstein is undeployed everywhere. If the real response disagrees with the assumed shape in some way the fixtures didn't anticipate, nothing in this gate — or in E1's — would have caught it. This is already the plan's own named ceiling (its "mandatory named follow-up": verify a genuinely-fresh, zero-history session the day Einstein deploys), restated here because it's the one thing that survives this step's own gate purely on trust, not proof.

## What Marcel is missing

The exact phrasing you just corrected in E2's docblock — asserting a step-E4 deletion as if already done — is still sitting, uncorrected, in E1's own **already-committed** docblock: `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx:49-50` reads "...fetched real product data for them via a dedicated utility — both deleted in build plan step E4 — instead of ever reading `useEinstein()`'s own `recommendations`," the identical ambiguous "deleted in build plan step E4" construction you just reworded here to make clearly future-tense. It's outside E2's diff so it doesn't move this verdict, but it's the same defect shape, in the same PR, one commit before the one where you fixed it — worth a one-line follow-up edit before this ships, since a reviewer who reads both files back-to-back will notice the inconsistency immediately.
